role: Topic Analyst — Governance, control structure and safety policy

topic.title: Governance, control structure and safety policy
topic.one_liner: Leaked draft prospectus, Sep 28: one Class F share gives seven founders 50.1% of votes and the Trust elects 4 of 7 directors. No public S-1 exists.

key_metrics.label: Founder vote share (Class F)
key_metrics.value: 50.1% of total voting power on key matters, one Class F share directed by a majority of seven co-founders (Reuters, T2). Holds while at least three keep a minimum stake, amount not reported. About 2% economic stake each (The Information, T3).

key_metrics.label: LTBT board-seat share
key_metrics.value: 4 of 7 seats (57%) elected by the Trust after IPO (Reuters, T2). Three of six named directors look Trust-linked today on the record's arithmetic (Hastings, Narasimhan, Liddell), so the fourth seat is open or unnamed. The T1 majority of Apr 14 reportedly lasted about five weeks (Kreps exit, T5).

key_metrics.label: Board size
key_metrics.value: 6 directors named in the draft prospectus: Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei (chair), Razavi, Hastings, Liddell, Narasimhan. 7 seats after IPO: 4 Trust, 3 Class F and Class A. Anthropic itself stated 6 members on Feb 13 and 7 on Apr 14.

key_metrics.label: Lock-up status
key_metrics.value: Unreported. No lock-up length in any opened prospectus coverage. The Information (Aug 27, Sep 3; T4 relays) says lock-ups beyond the standard 180 days are weighed, with insider sales in the offering and preset 10b5-1 plans for staff.

key_metrics.label: Trustees in office
key_metrics.value: 3 (Shah chair, Fontaine, Bernanke) versus 5 founding trustees on Sep 19, 2023. Four of five founders left by Jan 2026. Cuéllar left Aug 4, about 6.5 months after joining, to become Chief Global Affairs Officer.

key_metrics.label: RSP revision cadence
key_metrics.value: 9 versions since Sep 19, 2023. Five in 2026: v3.0 on Feb 24 to v3.4 on Jul 8, 19 weeks. v3.4 is the latest in the record, 84 days old at Sep 30.

what.t: Anthropic disclosed the Long-Term Benefit Trust on Sep 19, 2023 (T1). It holds Class T stock and was to elect a board majority within four years. Four of the five founding trustees have left: Matheny (Dec 2023), Christiano (Apr 2024), Bahl and Robinson (Jan 2026). Fontaine joined in 2025, Cuéllar in Jan 2026 (left Aug 4) and Bernanke in Jul 2026. Three trustees remain.

Trust-appointed directors arrived one at a time: Kreps May 29, 2024, Hastings May 28, 2025, Narasimhan Apr 14, 2026. Anthropic then said they were a majority of seven (T1). Kreps reportedly left about May 22 (T5, community sources). The draft prospectus names six directors: both Amodeis, Razavi, Hastings, Liddell, Narasimhan. Daniela Amodei chairs. Liddell's appointer is unstated.

Reuters' review of the draft prospectus (Sep 28 to 29, T2): a Founder LLC of seven co-founders directs one Class F share carrying 50.1% of votes on key matters. Class A gets one vote per share. The Trust elects four of seven directors. Four other classes exist, with minimal votes for strategic partners. Amazon's notes convert to nonvoting common at IPO, subject to an ownership cap (10-Q, T1).

RSP v1.0 (Sep 19, 2023) set ASL levels; changes needed board approval after Trust consultation. v2.0 (Oct 15, 2024) added capability thresholds. ASL-3 first applied to Opus 4 on May 22, 2025. v3.0 (Feb 24, 2026) turned hard commitments into non-binding targets. Four more followed by Jul 8; v3.2 gave the Trust review powers. v3.4 cut unredacted Risk Report sharing from all cleared staff to at least 200 employees.

No public S-1 exists on EDGAR (Sep 30). Reuters' review of the leaked draft (T2) confirms these themes: existential risk, shutdown resistance, concealment, blackmail-like behavior, evaluation awareness limiting safety tests, unsettled agent liability, and governance that may conflict with financial interests. About 6% of research compute went to safety in a July week (T3). Risk factors fill about 80 of 261 pages.

No lock-up term appears in any opened prospectus coverage. The Information (Aug 27, Sep 3; T4 relays of a T3 scoop) says lock-ups beyond 180 days are weighed, early investors and staff may sell in the offering, and rank-and-file staff may have to sell through preset 10b5-1 plans. Earlier liquidity: a May 2025 buyback at $61.5B (T3) and a Feb 2026 tender planned at $350B pre-money (T3).

means.t: Three instruments split control. The PBC charter lets directors weigh public benefit against financial interest, yet no decision or suit in the record cites it. Class T gives a no-equity Trust four seats. Class F gives seven founders, about 2% each (T3), half the vote by majority rule. Amazon and Google hold large stakes with no or minimal votes. Class A holders vote but cannot outvote Class F (inference).

The Trust's edge is seat math. Pre-IPO text (T1): trustees pick successors with Anthropic's input, serve one-year terms and hold no equity. Post-IPO amendment thresholds are not public. If measured on total votes, Class F can block any supermajority change (inference). Since Apr 2024 no trustee is described as an AI researcher, yet RSP v3.2 gave it review rights over Risk Reports. The board chair is also the President.

The RSP binds only by Anthropic's choice, and Anthropic rewrites it often. Three of the five 2026 revisions edited a capability threshold (v3.1, v3.3, v3.4). Roadmap goals are non-binding, higher-ASL safeguards may be 'outright impossible' to meet unilaterally, and v3.1 says Anthropic stays free to pause. No opened S-1 coverage mentions the RSP. California SB 53, in force Jan 1, 2026, adds a legal duty with its own framework.

Amodei refused 'any lawful use' terms on Feb 26. The federal ban followed Feb 27 (T1). N.D. Cal. vacated the 3252 label Aug 27; the D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion 2-1 Sep 25 (T1). A US export-control directive cut Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for 18 days from Jun 12 (T1). Sworn filings put lost DoD ARR at $150M (T2). Gross run-rate still passed $65B by end-July (T2).

implications.t: Reprice control, not mission. Treat Class A as a claim on economics with no route to a vote the founders oppose. Carry the Trust as a thin, self-perpetuating check until the public S-1 shows Class T amendment thresholds, the minimum-stake amount, sunset terms and the fourth Trust seat. Until then do not credit governance as a moat.

Score the RSP as disclosure plus outside review, not a covenant. Track Risk Reports, Trust-requested external reviews and the METR investigation, not ASL labels. A pause is a board choice under the PBC form, and about 80% of the $518B compute plan is non-cancelable or payable regardless of use (T2), so the pause option has a price.

Keep federal and export exposure as event risk in the model. Realized loss is small against run-rate: PitchBook put the ban near $200M, about 1.4% of ARR (T3), while sworn filings claim far more at risk, unrealized. Reprice on a second suspension, a FASCSA escalation or issued FTC demands.

Show every governance figure with its tier. Structure is leak-based (Reuters, T2) until EDGAR carries it. Show the Kreps exit (T5), about 2% per founder (T3) and lock-up ideas (T4) as unconfirmed, and gate the control metrics on the public S-1.

second_order: A single Class F share at 50.1% makes Class A votes irrelevant to any outcome the founders oppose, and Amazon and Google hold no or minimal votes. The live contest is founders versus Trust, not founders versus investors. Index committees and proxy advisers must rule on a powerless float. If Nasdaq-100 fast entry applies after 15 trading days (Business Insider, T3), passive funds would be buying within weeks.

The Trust gained RSP review powers on Apr 29, two weeks after its board majority, then lost the majority (reportedly May 22) and a trustee (Aug 4). Mandate rose as the bench thinned. The Trust must refill seats before a roadshow or the S-1 will describe three trustees and six sitting directors. This falsifies a reading of the four-year plan as a steady ramp in outside control.

Take-or-pay commitments make a pause expensive. About 80% of the $518B compute plan is non-cancelable or payable regardless of use (T2). Yet the draft reportedly says slowing the technology 'would likely be a good thing' (T3), and Anthropic backs a pause option (Jun 4) and slowing (Sep 12). A board that pauses still pays. Consensus reads the stance as free positioning. Class A holders would bear the cost without a deciding vote (inference).

Anthropic's June framework asked for legal authority to block dangerous deployments (dated Jun 1 in one record event, Jun 10 in another). A US export-control directive then cut two models on Jun 12, and Anthropic's reply asked for a statutory, transparent process (T1). On Anthropic's own account the dispute is process, not power. The White House hold on Mythos 5.1 (Sep 24) and the FTC probe (Sep 30) extend executive discretion that no Anthropic governance body can veto.

Liquidity design is supply management. Early insider sales, a lock-up beyond 180 days with a second window and preset 10b5-1 plans (T4 relays) would thin first-trade supply, next to a reported $10B Nvidia anchor, about 0.5% at $2T (T3). Underwriters must set the book. Amazon's nonvoting block, capped at an undisclosed level, sets the overhang. This bears on the absorption thesis.

watch.item: Public S-1 on EDGAR with Class F and Class T charter text, board section, lock-up and selling holders
watch.threshold: Reference class is this IPO's own filing history: three expected public-filing dates passed (end-Aug per Bloomberg, after Labor Day per The Information, late Sep per Reuters), none met by Sep 30. A filing by Oct 31 moves structure facts from T2 or T3 to T1. A later one supports the November-or-later reports (WSJ Sep 18; Reuters and Fortune Sep 29).

watch.item: Shareholder vote on the Class F special share and Founder LLC (Anthropic is asking shareholders, The Information via TechCrunch, Sep 25; no vote date reported)
watch.threshold: Approval on the reported terms (50.1%, three-founder test) confirms the structure. A change to 50.1%, the minimum stake or the sunset, or a named holder dissenting, signals bargaining. The approval threshold and which holders vote are not in the record.

watch.item: LTBT appointments: a successor for Cuéllar's trustee seat and the fourth Trust-elected director seat
watch.threshold: From the Trust's own record, the trustee count sat at three for over a year (Apr 2024 to mid-2025) and for about 6 months (Jan to Jul 2026). Different now: a prospectus must describe the seats. A named trustee or director before the roadshow shows refilling. None leaves three trustees and six directors.

watch.item: RSP v3.5 or later (latest in the record is v3.4 of Jul 8)
watch.threshold: 2026 cadence: five versions in 19 weeks, then none in the record for 84 days at Sep 30. A revision before the public S-1 changes what the prospectus must describe. Removing the Trust's v3.2 powers or the 'free to pause' language would contradict the governance narrative.

watch.item: Third Risk Report and the first Trust-requested external review
watch.threshold: The first report came Feb 2026 and the second Aug 14 (coverage date Jul 15). Stated cadence is 3 to 6 months, so the next is due Nov 14 2026 to Feb 14 2027 (desk arithmetic). A report after Feb 14 breaches the cadence. Any use of the Trust's review power shows it acts, not only holds it.

watch.item: Lock-up length, selling holders and Amazon's ownership cap in the public S-1
watch.threshold: Longer than 180 days with a staged release confirms The Information (T4 relays). A standard 180 days falsifies the supply-management reading. The DISPUTED flag on the Sep 3 event concerns raise size ($100B versus $130B), not lock-up. No lock-up base rate is in the record.

watch.item: Government levers: FASCSA en banc or cert petition, a DoD removal-complete statement, Commerce reimposition, issued FTC demands
watch.threshold: A petition keeps the exclusion contested through the listing. DoD says about 90% of workloads moved (T2, completion Sep 30 to end-October). A second Commerce suspension would make 18 days a repeat, not a one-off. No en banc or cert base rate is in the record.

watch.item: METR independent investigation of the four incidents (eight-week agreement, extendable)
watch.threshold: Eight weeks from Sep 9 ends Nov 4 (desk arithmetic; signing date not stated). A published finding with employee-level access supports the embedded-evaluator claim. An extension or silence before the roadshow leaves four incidents open as a risk factor.

topic.house_view: (a) Extends loosely: the reported $2T target is about 2.1x the $965B Series H and Reuters' analysis implies 18 to 20x sales, with no governance discount reported although Class A gets no control (targets, not a priced deal). (b) Touches: prospectus coverage records OpenAI's challenge to gross recognition and Anthropic's 'principal' position (Reuters, T3), so the dispute will sit in the S-1 text. (c) Extends: insider sales in the offering, lock-ups beyond 180 days and a reported $10B Nvidia anchor show supply is being managed (T3 and T4, unconfirmed). (d) Touches: $8.0B of Amazon notes convert to nonvoting common at IPO, so the rule must say how a converted note counts. (e) Confirms: governance conventions do not transfer, since the record names only Meta, Snap, Palantir and Veeva and none pairs a Trust with a PBC charter.

uncertainties.note: No public S-1 exists. Every structure fact is leak-based: Reuters' review (T2), Next Web and Jerusalem Post copies (T3), The Information scoops (T3). Not in the record: Class F and Class T charter text, minimum-stake amount, vote date, Class T amendment thresholds, Amazon's ownership cap, lock-up length, independence determinations, controlled-company status. Single-source: about 2% per founder and employee tie-break stock.

Board math is unresolved. Anthropic's Apr 14 post (T1) says Trust-appointed directors are a majority of seven. The May 22 Kreps exit rests on T5 community sources. Liddell's appointer is unstated. The prospectus says the Trust elects 4 of 7 while six directors are named. The seventh Founder LLC member is unnamed, and Anthropic calls Ben Mann a co-founder though the seven in The Information's account exclude him.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: An Anthropic board notice, the S-1 board section, or Kreps confirming the exit.

uncertainties.note: Moat versus liability is a judgment. There is no revenue counterfactual, run-rate is gross, the federal share is small (PitchBook about 1.4% of ARR, T3) and sworn claims of larger losses are unrealized. The courts split on cause. No win-loss data links safety posture to enterprise purchases, and the revenue effect of the 18-day suspension is undisclosed.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: S-1 customer and segment notes, federal revenue disclosure, or churn data.

uncertainties.note: RSP binding versus aspirational rests on Anthropic's own text and change log. No S-1 coverage mentions the RSP. Whether board approval after Trust consultation still governs v3.x changes is not stated. The Safeguards and pretraining resignations (Feb 9, T3; Sep 8, T2) are culture signals, not evidence of breach.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The S-1 safety governance section, the RSP amendment clause, or noncompliance reports.

uncertainties.note: Durability of founder control has no reference class in the record: only Meta, Snap and Palantir are named, without outcomes. Sunset is by attrition, at two or fewer founders, and none by date is reported. All seven pledged 80% of their equity to charity while three must keep a minimum stake; the interplay is not reported. Recalled, unverified: some US dual-class issuers adopt time-based sunsets.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Charter text, sunset and stake-test terms, pledge mechanics.

Export hold: Jun 12 directive suspended Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for 18 days; Jul 1 restoration with conditions; revenue effect not disclosed in any opened source.
Incident cluster: Jul 30 disclosure, Aug 31 overhaul with paused external cyber evals, Sep 9 assessment of four incidents and an eight-week METR investigation.
Pacing and outside evaluators: Sep 12 essay, Sep 18 Faculty named first embedded evaluator with at least $1B over five years, shared with Accenture.
Executive levers after the Pentagon ban: Sep 24 White House hold of Mythos 5.1 from UK AISI (T2) and Sep 30 FTC probe of Anthropic, OpenAI and METR (T2).
New T3 event: the draft S-1 leak item carries a reported prospectus quote that slowing the technology would likely be a good thing; Reuters original blocked, Crunchbase News relay.
Compute commitments of at least $518B with about 80% non-cancelable or payable regardless of use (Reuters, T2); used to price the pause option.
EDGAR check of Sep 30: no public Anthropic S-1; only a Jun 1 confidential draft (Rule 135 notice). All prospectus facts are leak-based.
Trustee count from ltbt table by date: 5 (Sep 2023), 4, 3 (Apr 2024), 4 (2025), 3 (Jan 2026), 4 (Jul 9 2026), 3 (Aug 4); matches the T1 'four members at the time' on the Bernanke post.
rsp table against events: nine versions; v3.0 Feb 24 to v3.4 Jul 8 is 134 days, 19.1 weeks, matching the desk note of five revisions in 19 weeks. Gap from Jul 8 to Sep 30 is 84 days.
offering_structure against prospectus_facts: 50.1%, seven founders, Trust four of seven and Class A one vote agree across Reuters (T2) and The Information (T3).
Searched every prospectus_facts and risk_factor_themes row for RSP, ASL and Responsible Scaling: zero hits. The RSP is absent from prospectus coverage in the record.
Arithmetic: 7 founders x about 2% is about 14% economics against 50.1% votes, about 3.6x (single-source T3 input). Seats: 4 of 7 is 57%; 3 of 6 is 50%. 80 of 261 pages is 30.7%.
Amazon holdings: record's desk arithmetic ($97.9B + $92.5B) over $965B gives about 19.7%. TheStreet says 15% to 20% and Forkast about 21% (T4); Amazon discloses no percentage.
Checked the board table: Kreps row is T1 for joining but its exit date rests on T5 sources; Liddell appointer 'unknown' in the table. Both match the open items.

Board majority conflict: Anthropic's Apr 14 post (T1) says Trust-appointed directors are a majority of seven; a May 22 Kreps exit (T5) would leave 3 of 6. Liddell's appointer is unstated, so both readings stand.
Seat count gap: the draft prospectus names six directors but describes seven seats (4 Trust, 3 Class F and A). A vacancy or an unnamed director is implied; the record does not say which.

Founder roster mismatch: The Information's seven (Fortune list) exclude Ben Mann, whom Anthropic's Jan 13 2026 post calls a co-founder; the Jan 2021 founding event lists eight names. The seventh Founder LLC member is unnamed in every opened Reuters copy.

Stale open item: desk-s1 lists the PBC and LTBT governance risk text as not quoted in any opened coverage, but the Reuters quote on governance conflicting with financial interests is recorded on the Sep 29 Class F event.

Structured-field error risk: the Sep 25 founder-control event carries valuation_post_usd_m 1,500,000, a secondary-market mark that its own note says is not a priced round. Series H remains $965B post-money.

Duplicate scoop with split tiers: the Aug 18 super-voting report is one event at T2 HIGH (Reuters relay) and another at T3 MEDIUM (The Information via Investing.com). I treat it as a T3 single-source scoop and anchor on the Sep 28 to 29 Reuters review.
RSP v2.2 (May 14 2025) excluded sophisticated and state-compromised insiders from the ASL-3 security standard eight days before ASL-3 was first activated (May 22 2025).

Safety compute share has two descriptions: about 6% of research compute in a July sample week (Reuters on the prospectus) and about 6% of capacity plus 12% safety-focused AI R&D (SiliconANGLE on Anthropic's Sep 17 post, unopened). Bases differ.
Essay date split: the June 'Policy on the AI Exponential' framework sits in two events dated Jun 1 (T1 HIGH) and Jun 10 (T1 MEDIUM, date inferred from coverage).
The Sep 3 lock-up event carries DISPUTED confidence. The dispute is raise size ($130B versus $100B) and Q2 figures, not the lock-up wording, which stays T4.

Unaddressed interplay: all seven founders pledged 80% of personal equity to charity (Reuters, T2) while the Class F test needs three founders to keep a minimum stake and a founder drops out for selling too many shares.

Amazon's $8.0B of notes convert to nonvoting common at IPO subject to an undisclosed cap. The capital-efficiency rule needs a stated treatment of converted notes. Lock-up and any secondary component are T4 only.

Governance and safety as moat evidence: regulated-industry safeguards (Sep 1) and Fortune 10 customers exist, but no win-loss data ties safety posture to purchases. Government outcomes are discretionary.
Legal hooks: the governance risk-factor quote, agent-liability language, the Sep 18 Sherman Act suit citing the pacing essay, and the Sep 30 FTC probe. Class F charter text is not public.

Bull-usable facts with tiers: Trust-elected majority reached 17 months early (T1), outside evaluators funded at $1B over five years (shared), SB 53 compliance framework, revenue kept growing through the Pentagon dispute.
